sources.quote: Statistics Canada reported that 58% of children aged 0 to 5 were in some form of child care in 2025, centre-based care most common at about 32%
sources.title: The Daily — Child care arrangements, 2025
sources.evidence: In 2025, 58% of children aged 0 to 5 years were in child care in Canada. Centre-based child care remained the most common type of arrangement in 2025, with 32% of all children aged 0 to 5 using this type of child care, followed by care by a relative (12%) and home-based child care (10%). 31% of parents of children aged 0 to 5 years reported that their child was on a waitlist in 2025, up from 26% in 2023.

sources.quote: Quebec's Childcare Services Registration Portal, which replaced La Place 0-5 in November 2025
sources.publisher: Gouvernement du Québec (Ministère de la Famille)
sources.title: Childcare Services Registration Portal (formerly La Place 0-5) | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: The Childcare Services Registration Portal replaced La Place 0-5, marking an important step toward a more equitable and transparent allocation of spaces in CPEs and subsidized day care centres. Following the closure of La Place 0-5 on October 16, approximately 250,000 child files were transferred to the Childcare Services Registration Portal. Parents had access to the new registration portal at the beginning of November.

sources.quote: prenatal registration is gone, and rank keys off the desired start date, not the sign-up date
sources.title: Un nouveau portail d'inscription pour une attribution plus équitable et transparente des places en services de garde Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: Only children already born, or arrived in their families in the case of adoption, can be registered. For the allocation of spaces, the desired date of entry into childcare is now what will be taken into account, rather than the date of registration on the platform.

sources.title: Find childcare | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: The Childcare Search tool allows you to find active, licensed Alberta childcare programs near you. It provides information on licensed childcare programs and family day home agencies, including 18 months of non-compliance history. Results include the facility name, full address, phone number, capacity, accreditation status and previous inspections.

sources.quote: never let staff write reviews: Google prohibits gating and incentives
sources.publisher: Google Maps User Generated Content Policy Help
sources.title: Prohibited & restricted content - Maps User Generated Content Policy Help
sources.evidence: Google prohibits offering incentives such as payment, discounts, free goods and/or services in exchange for posting any review or revision or removal of a negative review, and also prohibits discouraging or prohibiting negative reviews or selectively soliciting positive reviews from customers.

sources.quote: The same rules cap them at five children under 13
sources.title: Home child care and unlicensed child care: how many children are allowed | Government of Ontario
sources.evidence: If you are an unlicensed child care program provider, you can have a maximum of 5 children under 13 years old. You must inform parents/guardians that you are an unlicensed provider in writing, stating: This child care program is not licensed by the Government of Ontario. You must keep a copy of your written notification on file for 2 years.

sources.quote: Licensed Ontario centres in CWELCC may not charge eligible families more than the capped daily fee
sources.title: Child care centre licensing manual, Part 2: Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) | Government of Ontario
sources.evidence: Base fees for eligible children in CWELCC-enrolled child care programs must now be $22 per day or less. On January 1, 2025, specific rules took effect for programs already enrolled in CWELCC. CWELCC-enrolled licensees must consider all mandatory fees charged to parents/guardians when calculating their overall base fee, including registration fees and any other one-time or recurring fees.

sources.quote: Ontario banned waiting list fees and deposits in 2016
sources.title: Ontario ending fees for child care wait lists | Government of Ontario
sources.evidence: On September 1, 2016, new provisions to Ontario Regulation 137/15 banned child care wait list fees. Ontario Regulation 137/15 prohibits child care centres from charging a waiting list fee or deposit to parents seeking to be added to or removed from a waiting list.

sources.quote: are titles restricted to members of the College of Early Childhood Educators
sources.title: About RECEs | Welcome to the College of Early Childhood Educators
sources.evidence: Only registered members of the College of Early Childhood Educators can legally practise the profession of early childhood education and use the protected titles registered early childhood educator (RECE), early childhood educator (ECE) and their French equivalents. It is an offence under the ECE Act for an individual who is not a member in good standing of the College to use the protected titles, with a fine of up to $5,000 for a first offence.

sources.quote: standard benefits run up to 40 weeks within a 52-week window and the extended option stretches to roughly 18 months
sources.title: Digest of Benefit Entitlement Principles Chapter 13 - Section 1 - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: The maximum shareable standard parental benefits is 40 weeks, and the standard parental benefits window begins with the week in which the child is born or placed with the claimant for purposes of adoption and ends 52 weeks after that week. The maximum shareable extended parental benefits is 69 weeks, and the extended parental benefits window ends 78 weeks after that week.
